Marcus — thanks for the walkthrough earlier. The procurement committee asked me to get a clearer picture of the ordering of dependencies between the MSA, DPA and order form so we can line up our legal and security review windows.

Can you confirm:
- Which document needs to be fully signed before we can start the pilot?
- Is the DPA a gating item or can it be handled in parallel with trial data workflows under the MSA?
- Do you have a suggested milestone-based close timeline we can share with procurement?

We're trying to lock calendar windows for our internal approvers; any concise map you can send would help.

Thanks,
Sylvia Park
Head of IT Procurement
Maven Biotech

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sylvia Park <sylvia.park@mavenbiotech.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff & sequencing questions

Hi Sylvia — appreciate the clear questions. I've sketched an "accordion"-style MAP that keeps acceptance milestones and legal gating visible while allowing parallel workstreams where safe. See attached MAP-v2.xlsx (tabbed by legal/security/prod). High level answers below:

1) Pilot start: we prefer an executed MSA + minimal Order Form (pilot scope + SOW) in place before provisioning. That protects both parties for IP and liability.

2) DPA: treated as a gating item for pilot data ingestion into our hosted environment. We can run a sandbox pilot with synthetic data while DPA review is progressing, but any PHI/real data requires DPA + controls validated.

3) Suggested close timeline (high level):
   - Week 0 (contract kickoff): finalize pilot SOW + draft MSA and DPA concurrently.
   - Weeks 1-2: legal redlines and security questionnaire.
   - Weeks 3-4: executive signoff window; procurement issues PO/order workflow.
   - Week 5: provisioning and pilot execution.

Next steps: I attached MAP-v2.xlsx and a heatmap export that Neha will circulate for dependency detail. Can you confirm your procurement approver names + earliest contract-sign window so we can align our sales/legal?

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-v2.xlsx (mutual action plan draft)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sylvia Park <sylvia.park@mavenbiotech.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T10:23:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff & sequencing questions — dependency heatmap

Posted the more granular dependency heatmap as PDF (attached). Pulling out the items I expect procurement will ask for:

- Acceptance criteria matrix (SLA/latency/uptime acceptance for pilot) — owned by Product (we will draft).
- Data handling checklist mapped to DPA clauses (encryption at rest/in-transit, retention windows, deletion SLA).
- Order form fields required for PO: billing entity, tax ID, billing contact, billing lead time.
- Escrow / termination window language — usually legal asks for standard 90-day termination notice or mutual acceptance gates.

Key note: To keep timeline tight we recommend a staggered signature approach ("accordion"):
   1) Sign pilot Order Form + MSA (operational baseline)
   2) Finalize DPA and attach as amendment (if your legal needs a longer review cycle)
   3) Execute full commercial order form for production scale after pilot acceptance criteria met

I've flagged items in the heatmap that need Sylvia's legal contact to confirm. Marcus — can you add the DocuSign envelope link once we freeze the MSA text?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Manager, Security & Compliance Ops
Redwood Inference
